questions.solution:
s1 works as a mutex, so whichever thread gets s1 first runs its part first.

T1 first: wait(s1), x = 1, print 1, then wait(s2) blocks (s2 = 0) while holding s1. T2 blocks on wait(s1) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] deadlock, only "1" printed. So option 3 is possible and option 1 is not.

T2 first: wait(s1), x = 1, print 1, signal(s2), signal(s1). Then T1: x = 2, print 2, wait(s2) succeeds, signal(s1). So option 2 is possible; T2 never blocks, so option 4 is not.

Answer: Options 2 and 3

options: T1 runs first and prints 1, T2 runs next and prints 2
T2 runs first and prints 1, T1 runs next and prints 2
T1 runs first and prints 1, T2 does not print anything (deadlock)
T2 runs first and prints 1, T1 does not print anything (deadlock)

questions.text: Let [latex]A[/latex]  be an [latex] n \times n[/latex]  matrix over the set of all real numbers [latex]R[/latex]. Let [latex]B[/latex]  be a matrix obtained from [latex]A[/latex] by swapping two rows. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Swapping two rows changes the sign of the determinant: [latex]\det B=-\det A[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- So [latex]\det A\ne0\Rightarrow\det B\ne0[/latex]: B is invertible [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&3\end{bmatrix}[/latex] is symmetric, but [latex]B=\begin{bmatrix}2&3\\1&2\end{bmatrix}[/latex] is not [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{bmatrix}[/latex] has trace 0, but [latex]B=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}[/latex] has trace 1 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Options 1 and 2

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The determinant of [latex]B[/latex] is the negative of the determinant of [latex]A[/latex]
If [latex]A[/latex] is invertible, then [latex]B[/latex] is also invertible
If [latex]A[/latex] is symmetric, then [latex]B[/latex] is also symmetric
If the trace of [latex]A[/latex] is zero, then the trace of [latex]B[/latex] is also zero

questions.text:
Let S1 and S2 be two stacks. S1 has capacity of 4 elements. S2 has capacity of 2 elements. S1 already has 4 elements: 100, 200, 300, and 400, whereas S2 is empty, as shown below.

[latex] \begin{array}{|c|} \hline 400 (Top) \\ \hline 300 \\ \hline 200\\ \hline 100 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
Stack S1

[latex] \begin{array}{|c|} \hline \\ \hline \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
Stack S2

Only the following three operations are available:

PushToS2: Pop the top element from S1 and push it on S2.
PushToS1: Pop the top element from S2 and push it on S1.
GenerateOutput: Pop the top element from S1 and output it to the user.

Note that the pop operation is not allowed on an empty stack and the push operation is not allowed on a full stack.

Which of the following output sequences can be generated by using the above operations?
questions.solution:
S1 = 100, 200, 300, 400 (top). S2 can hold only 2 elements.

- 100, 200, 400, 300: to output 100 first, 400, 300, 200 (3 elements) must go to S2 [latex]\text{---}[/latex] impossible.
- 200, 300, 400, 100: move 400, 300 to S2; output 200; move 300 back, output 300; move 400 back, output 400; output 100 True
- 400, 200, 100, 300: output 400; move 300 to S2; output 200, 100; move 300 back, output 300 True
- 300, 200, 400, 100: move 400 to S2; output 300, 200; move 400 back, output 400; output 100 True

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4

questions.text: Which of the following is/are EQUAL to 224 in radix-5 (i.e., base-5) notation?
questions.solution:
[latex](224)_5=2\times25+2\times5+4=64[/latex]

- [latex](64)_{10}=64[/latex] True
- [latex](100)_8=64[/latex] True
- [latex](50)_{16}=80[/latex] False
- [latex](121)_7=49+14+1=64[/latex] True

Answer: 64 in radix-10, 100 in radix-8, 121 in radix-7

questions.text:
Consider 4-variable functions [latex] f 1, f 2, f 3, f 4 [/latex] expressed in sum-of-minterms form as given below.
[latex] \begin{aligned} & f 1=\sum(0,2,3,5,7,8,11,13) \\ & f 2=\sum(1,3,5,7,11,13,15) \\ & f 3=\sum(0,1,4,11) \\ & f 4=\sum(0,2,6,13) \end{aligned} [/latex]


With respect to the circuit given above, which of the following options is/are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Compute the AND, OR and XOR outputs as minterm sets:
- AND: [latex]f_1\cdot f_2[/latex] = common minterms = [latex]\{3,5,7,11,13\}[/latex]
- OR: [latex]f_3+f_4=\{0,1,4,11\}\cup\{0,2,6,13\}=\{0,1,2,4,6,11,13\}[/latex]
- XOR keeps minterms present in exactly one of them: [latex]\{3,5,7\}\cup\{0,1,2,4,6\}[/latex]; 11 and 13 are in both, so they drop.

[latex]Y=\Sigma(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7)=\Pi(8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15)[/latex] (i.e. [latex]Y=\bar A[/latex]).

Answer: [latex]Y=\Sigma(0,\ldots,7)[/latex] and [latex]Y=\Pi(8,\ldots,15)[/latex]
